title: Unawareness during account registration
description: Homeowner (EE1) shares personal details and device info without full awareness of how the Home Hub will process, store, or share that data long-term.

title: Disclosure of enrollment data
description: Home Hub (P1) receives and stores identifiable account and camera/sensor enrollment data, risking disclosure if access controls or encryption fail.

title: Identifiability through registration metadata
description: The flow itself carries metadata that can identify the homeowner and link them to specific home devices being enrolled.
uncertainty_note: Context mapping lists I at fl but exact tree node is inferred from standard LINDDUN Pro trees.

title: Detecting guest involvement via observed code entry
description: An observer can detect the guest user's participation or presence by observing the communication (entering the temporary access code at the Home Hub), without needing access to the data itself.
assumptions: Physical or side-channel observation of the entry action is possible.
uncertainty_note: Based on context [5] about observed communication for Detecting threats.

title: Non-repudiation of door access
description: The Home Hub (process) may record the use of the temporary access code, creating evidence that prevents the guest from denying their access to the front door.
assumptions: Access events are logged by the system.

title: Guest unawareness of access logging
description: The guest user may be unaware of how their temporary code entry is processed, stored, or potentially shared by the Home Hub, leading to unawareness of privacy implications.
assumptions: No explicit privacy notice is given at the time of code entry.

title: Linkability of events in local log
description: The Home Hub writing sensor events to the Local Event Log enables linking of motion/door activations over time, revealing household activity patterns and routines.
assumptions: Log is persistent and can be queried or accessed by processes or users.

title: Disclosure of sensitive sensor data
description: Storing detailed motion, door, and sensor events in the local log discloses private information about inhabitants' presence, movements, and behaviors if the datastore is accessed unauthorized.
assumptions: Events contain personal or identifiable activity data.
uncertainty_note: Context confirms Process->DataStore allows Dd at D but specific tree node chosen by judgement.

title: Unawareness of event logging
description: Home Hub (P1) writes events without ensuring users are aware that their sensor activities are being persistently logged locally.
assumptions: Users may not have been informed or consented to detailed logging.

title: Disclosure of personal video data
description: The cloud storage receives and stores recorded camera clips which contain personal and potentially sensitive information about household members and activities. Insufficient access controls or breaches can lead to unauthorized disclosure of private home footage.

title: Linkability via upload metadata
description: Metadata from the upload flow (e.g., timing, frequency, account identifiers) can link multiple video clips to the same household or user, enabling activity profiling.

title: Unawareness of continuous data upload
description: Users operating the Home Hub may not fully realize or consent to the extent of video clips being automatically uploaded and retained in the cloud.

title: Motion alert data disclosure to backend
description: The real-time motion alert contains personal data about home occupancy and activity; forwarding it to the Mobile App Backend discloses this to the service provider, which may be an excessive or unintended exposure depending on user expectations and data minimality.
assumptions: Motion alerts are considered personal data as they reveal behavioral patterns in a private home setting.
uncertainty_note: Context emphasizes Dd.4 for involved parties/exposure; applies here as transfer to backend (potentially external party) but exact system boundaries not specified in flow.

title: Disclosure of motion events via push notification
description: The backend pushes a notification containing details of detected motion (implying presence/activity at the homeowner's property) to the phone; if the channel or notification service is compromised or logged, this sensitive personal data is disclosed.
assumptions: Notification payload includes event details; push service or network path is not fully trusted/encrypted end-to-end.

title: Detectability of home activity notifications
description: Existence and timing of push notifications from the backend to the homeowner's device can be observed (e.g., via network traffic analysis or notification service logs), revealing patterns of motion/activity at the home without needing to read the content.
assumptions: Adversary can monitor network or has access to push notification metadata.
uncertainty_note: Context does not explicitly cover notification metadata threats; based on general LINDDUN detectability for data flows.

title: Linkability of motion events to homeowner identity at backend
description: By sending the notification, the Mobile App Backend (P2) links the specific motion-detection event to the particular homeowner's account/device, enabling profiling of home occupancy patterns.
assumptions: Backend maintains user-to-device mapping for push delivery.

title: Unawareness of data sharing with analytics vendor
description: Mobile app backend shares aggregated device-usage analytics without ensuring end-users are fully aware of the data collection and sharing practices with the external cloud analytics vendor.
assumptions: Users of the mobile app may not have been informed about analytics sharing in privacy policy or consent flows.

title: Disclosure of usage analytics to third party
description: Cloud analytics vendor receives and processes aggregated device-usage data, which could lead to unintended disclosure or secondary use of patterns that might be re-identifiable.
assumptions: Even aggregated data can sometimes be linked back to individuals or groups when combined with other datasets.
uncertainty_note: Aggregation reduces but does not eliminate all privacy risks; context may vary.

title: Linkability via analytics flow metadata
description: The data flow itself reveals communication between the mobile app backend and cloud analytics vendor, enabling linkability of app usage to specific third-party analytics services.
assumptions: Network observers or the vendor could use metadata to link app instances or users to analytics tracking.

title: Violation of storage limitation principle upon retrieval
description: Mobile app backend (P2) receives the video clip and may store or cache it longer than needed for the playback purpose, violating storage limitation.
assumptions: The backend process might retain the retrieved clip in logs, cache or temporary storage beyond immediate playback needs.
uncertainty_note: Context example of insufficient minimization upon storing at recipient applies here; exact retention policy not specified in flow description.
